P1.evidence: Setter notes read back properly and the handoff acknowledged: 'so I had a chat with Kim I think you spoke to him the other day right... I kind of have like a brief of what's been going on with you but I'm definitely an old school guy and I'd love to hear it from you.' The frame carried two of four parts — where you are and what help you need — and agreement was only a trailing 'yeah totally' rather than a sought confirmation. The open question ran cleanly: 'what's going on and like what how can we actually help you with your fitness health and overall.'

P2.evidence: The thinnest physical baseline in the batch. No age, no height, no weight — none of the three exist anywhere in this transcript, on a six-month body transformation. Health conditions were never asked. Most significantly P2d was never asked either: there was no injury or limitation question at any point, even though the prospect twice volunteered back problems — 'my back is not working great' and 'I would love if my low back wasn't the first thing to go' — and works a job holding a 30lb camera at height for ninety minutes at a stretch. That question ran on almost every other call in this batch and is simply absent here. What did run ran well: work was explored thoroughly and usefully, down to the tour cadence and its effect on sleep and food; diet was asked with a processed-food follow-up; and sleep was asked and pursued properly — 'you mentioned your sleep is off. Is that still the thing?' — which surfaced the most useful proof point on the call, that his sleep improved within a week of starting kettlebell work.

P3.evidence: Contains the single best question asked anywhere in this batch. The prospect said he had lost respect for himself and, instead of moving on, the rep stopped and pushed: 'Why would you say, it's a powerful word to use to lose respect for... So why would you say that?' That produced a two-minute unguarded self-diagnosis naming the exact gap the product addresses. The what-does-that-give-you question also ran and landed: 'tell me, how are you actually feeling when you're pushing through that, the discomfort... when you finish the workout?' drawing 'the confidence thing, I'm like, I like that guy, that guy can stick it through.' The reflect-back was excellent and explicitly confirmed — 'you're on a journey right now that you don't need motivation to actually do it. It's more of a structure how to do it, actually, properly. Would that be a fair assessment?' / 'Yep.' Identity was reached in full. What is missing is the social layer: nobody asked who else this impacts, and the girlfriend appears once, incidentally. Aesthetics was never asked, which is defensible here since the prospect explicitly deprioritised it.

P4.evidence: The root cause phase effectively ran inside P3 and it ran well. The prospect named why nothing stuck, unprompted and precisely: 'the only times I would go pick up a jump rope or pick up a kettlebell... the only times I would say yes are when I felt it, felt the motivation.' He named the blocker: 'I don't know how to say no to things that I want to say no to, and I don't know how to say yes to the things I don't want to say yes to, like picking up a weight.' And he named the gap and the solution himself: 'I want help from people who have walked this path before and who know how to do it well... I want a coach. That's what I want.' The rep's reflect-back served the function of P4f without using the scripted line. Past attempts and outcomes surfaced narratively rather than being asked for, which is why P4a and P4b are partial.

P5.evidence: Never run. No two-year question, no settle question, no 'why not', no line in the sand. The rep did spend several minutes on a discomfort philosophy — the Andy Frisella quote, 'tell me one thing in your life that is great that came as a result of being comfortable', the lottery winners, the snooze button — and it landed hard ('That's so good... Damn. I was even thinking about tattooing it'). But that is motivational framing about the value of discomfort, not a consequence frame about the cost of inaction, and none of the four checks ran. Nine calls into this batch, P5 has not been run once.

P6.evidence: The belief check was a general temperature read — 'What are your thoughts on that? This is how the whole thing is structured' — which drew the most enthusiastic response of the call. The all-in question never ran. P6c is nonetheless a clear hit: the yes was unambiguous and the prospect supplied it before being asked, then drove the close himself with 'Are we going to move forward right now?' No hesitation existed to return to Phase 5 for.

P11.evidence: Payment collected and confirmed by both sides. Onboarding booked for Monday July 27 at 3:15pm Central and read back by the prospect from the confirmation email. Step three fails outright and by the rep's own choice: the agreement arrived and was acknowledged, and the rep then explicitly deferred the signature — 'So you don't have to do it right now. You just need to sign it before the session with Trevor. I don't want to keep you any longer.' The check requires having them sign it on the call, so this is a miss rather than a partial. Step four is partial: the onboarding form was named but Primal University and the community were never mentioned at all, unlike every other closed call in this batch.

objection_plays.detail: Soft trigger, honestly stated: 'because I've been taking the summer off, and I haven't had income since May, I feel more drawn to being able to finance it.' The rep did not isolate first and ran no should-versus-how frame. He did run one financial-picture move — 'What's your credit score? Do you know?' — the second time in this batch, and then laddered three structures. Handled well in one respect: the interest-free in-house three-pay was offered first and the prospect took it immediately, so the buyer landed on the cheapest option rather than being routed to external credit as happened on the Beau Paschall and Patrick Dominguez calls. Handled poorly in another: the prospect had just said he has no income until September, and nobody checked that two of the three monthly payments fall inside that window. The rest of the financial picture — cash on hand, monthly surplus, cards, available credit, investments — never ran.
No think-about-it trigger. The prospect asked to move forward before the rep proposed it.
No spouse or partner consult raised, despite a girlfriend being mentioned.
No timing objection, even though he returns to touring in September. He treated the tour as a constraint to design around rather than a reason to delay.
No fear or doubt about the programme or the provider. He had been following the coach's free content for weeks and had already validated it on his own body.

SCRIPT GAP — nutrition without food control. From September to December the prospect eats catered tour food four or five nights a week and has no say in it: 'sometimes these catered meals are just not clean food at all. And I just won't eat.' The rep answered with guidelines plus sourcing his own food near where he is stationed, which does not address the nights when that is impossible, and the prospect explicitly left it open — 'just to put that on the table, that is one caveat.' The playbook has no move for a client whose food environment is controlled by an employer, and this affects roughly half the six-month term.

SCRIPT GAP handled well — a direct policy question about alcohol during the six months. No scripted answer exists and the rep improvised honestly: no prohibition ('he cannot prohibit anything, right'), his own ten years without drinking as an example rather than an instruction, a nutritional rationale, and a permissive caveat. The prospect accepted it without friction. Worth capturing as a standard answer, since it is the second policy question in this batch the script does not cover.

notes: Best discovery on the emotional axis and worst on the physical axis, in the same call. The self-respect question and the reflect-back that followed should be lifted as training material — one question moved this from a fitness conversation to an identity conversation and the close followed almost automatically. But no age, height, weight or injury question was asked at all, on a six-month transformation for a man who twice mentioned his low back failing first. Two fixes: run the injury screen even when the prospect is young and enthusiastic, and stop deferring the agreement signature — P11c has now been deferred or left unconfirmed on every closed call in this batch.
